one_line: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to Southeast Asia under new rules while memory shortages drive hardware costs higher.

themes.title: Export controls and chip shortages hit hardware supply chain
themes.text: Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to halt AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries following new U.S. export controls. Meanwhile, global memory chip shortages are causing price spikes, and the Netherlands is moving to block a U.S. bill restricting ASML sales in China.

stories.headline: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries
Memory chip shortages spark global procurement war rooms and 10x price hikes
Netherlands seeks to block US MATCH Act restricting ASML China sales
Avicena raises $100M+ Series C for microLED optical interconnects
SoftBank default risk hits 4-year high amid AI investment worries

themes.title: Workforce restructuring and AI job displacement projections
themes.text: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 positions to shift its business toward artificial intelligence. Concurrently, a JP Morgan report estimates that AI could displace 24 million knowledge-worker jobs globally over five years.

stories.headline: SAP prepares plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions for AI shift
AI could displace 24 million knowledge-worker jobs in five years: JP Morgan
Dante Security raises $10M seed to monitor enterprise AI agents

themes.title: New model releases and Google Workspace agent mandates
themes.text: BharatGen and Chariot AI launched new open-weight and multimodal model suites under India's national AI initiatives. Additionally, Google mandated that Workspace AI agents use Model Context Protocol servers starting February 2027.

stories.headline: BharatGen launches Patram 1.5, a 7B vision-language model for documents
Chariot AI unveils Chariot-1 LLM and speech models under IndiaAI Mission
Google mandates MCP server access for Workspace AI agents by February 2027

themes.title: State-backed hackers adopt AI tools as data leaks emerge
themes.text: State-backed hackers from China and North Korea integrated the AI-powered penetration testing platform Artex into their attack workflows. Separately, confidential data sent to Chinese startup MiniMax was accessed by unidentified parties despite requests for data deletion.

stories.headline: China and North Korean state-backed hackers add AI tool Artex to their arsenals
Confidential data sent to Chinese AI startup MiniMax accessed by unknown parties
